MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-10-29; reviewed_by stays null): status changed from blocked SDK_BUG to pass. The author found a real SDK defect: MujocoDriver declared only observation and tick while the MuJoCo bridge publishes time_ms, qpos, qvel, ctrl, tick, timestep_ms and seed (G6.READ_INVALID), and an empty reset schema published the catalogue class's undescribed fields (G8.NO_DESCRIPTION). Both are fixed in the SDK (MHS/changes/WAVE-A.md); the reviewer removed the package's reset workaround where it had one, regenerated the reference and re-ran the gate. After the registry rebuild the reviewer re-ran the gate and wrote its digest above. The author's notes as written at the time of the block follow.

BLOCKED ON AN SDK DEFECT OF THE MUJOCO FAMILY, not on this repository. Last gate output (trimmed): G1 pass Layout and isolation; G2 pass Lock; G3 pass Strict resolve; G4 pass Provenance; G5 pass Reference; G6 fail Behaviour with warning G6.NOT_RECORDED (expected: the fake backend is the package's stand-in for the mujoco library, so native calls are not recorded) and error G6.READ_INVALID 'the resource state does not match its state_schema: $.time_ms: additional property time_ms is not allowed (allowed: "observation", "tick")'; G7 warn Native surface with warning G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND (expected, same reason); G8 warn Protocol and surface with G8.NO_UNIT x2 (the integer inputs ticks and action.ctrl that the bridge derives; PLAYBOOK section 8 calls these warnings expected for simulator families); G9 NOT_RUN (skipped after the G6 failure). MINIMAL REPRO, no package needed: build any MujocoDriver with a stand-in mujoco module (MHS/sdk/tests/bridges/support.py:fake_mujoco() is enough), build its manifest, serve it, read the world resource and validate the state against the published state_schema. The schema has the properties {observation, tick} (MHS/sdk/src/mhs/driver/families.py:838-843, MujocoDriver._state_fields) while MujocoBridge.world_state returns {time_ms, qpos, qvel, ctrl, tick, timestep_ms, seed} (MHS/sdk/src/mhs/bridge/mujoco.py:329-342), so the schema validator reports six 'additional property' errors (time_ms, qpos, qvel, ctrl, timestep_ms, seed) and G6 fails READ_INVALID for every package of the family. The SDK's own MujocoDriver tests do not catch it because they never run the gate (MHS/sdk/tests/driver/test_families.py:406-419). A FIX makes one side match the other: return the bridge's keys from MujocoDriver._state_fields, or nest world_state under 'observation' and keep 'tick'. SECOND SDK GAP, worked around in this package without touching the SDK: the family leaves the reset inputs undescribed (MHS/sdk/src/mhs/driver/families.py:711-716, _SimDriver._RESET_INPUTS is empty for MuJoCo, unlike GymnasiumDriver), so G8.NO_DESCRIPTION failed for seed, scenario and options; this package declares cap.world.reset.v1 in its `actions` with described fields, and after that only the expected unit warnings remain. WHAT THE PACKAGE IS: the card's main model (models[0], aloha_sim/assets/aloha/aloha_pbr.xml) served as a MujocoDriver in simulated mode R0: the step action is data.ctrl bounded per actuator by the model's actuator_ctrlrange (14 position actuators, seven per arm), the reset restores the model defaults, the state is the model's integration state, and the fidelity contract (F1, lockstep, realtime_factor 0) is published with its gaps. The model file is read from the read-only clone in place; neither the model nor its assets are copied. WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER: MuJoCo itself, which was not installed and cannot be installed where the gate runs (no network, no pip); the fake backend (fake.py) parses the card's MJCF text for the model shape but integrates a placeholder first-order motion of each actuated joint toward its control target, resolves no mesh, contact, equality or tendon constraint, and was never compared with the real engine; no rendering; no physical ALOHA robot is modelled and nothing was validated against hardware. The package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null). backends['fake'] in driver.py is the class object fake.FakeMujoco (the stand-in mujoco module, the form the SDK's own MujocoDriver tests use, MHS/sdk/tests/driver/test_families.py:399-403), which is why G7 reports UPSTREAM_BACKEND; driver.lock.json names it as .fake:FakeMujoco. This package is otherwise complete for the fake backend: reference generated, test_driver.py keeps the check_driver call and adds six cases (model shape from the card model, per-actuator control-range refusals, state follows the control target, reset to the model defaults, published fidelity contract, e-stop latch), and those cases pass. It will need one gate run again after the SDK fix.

MODEL REVIEW (gpt-6, a model and not a human, 2026-11-02; reviewed_by stays null): Accepted the shared MuJoCo checkpoint v2 migration after independent codec review and this actual G1-G9 fake gate rerun. Regenerated the declared native_checkpoint field and conservative derived determinism; state API presence no longer implies seeded or exact continuation. The explicit basic fallback does not claim complete integration state. Earlier automatically inferred determinism is superseded by the current reference. Changed reference.json, REFERENCE.md, check-report.json, RESULT.json. Source pin, package model authorship and driver.lock.json are unchanged. No native runtime of this package or physical hardware was validated; isolated SDK engine tests are separate evidence.
